# A package of the main module compiles under the same key in every checkout.
# Its compile names its source by module path, as -trimpath does. The link
# puts the directory back, so a binary names the files of its own checkout.

env GOCACHE=$WORK/gocache
mkdir $GOCACHE

go list -export -f '{{.ImportPath}} {{.BuildID}}' ./... other.example/part
stdout '^m/leaf '
stdout '^other.example/part '
cp stdout $WORK/first.txt
go vet -x ./leaf
stderr 'vet\.cfg'
go build -o $WORK/first.exe ./cmd/where
cd cmd/where
exec $WORK/first.exe
cd ../..

# The second checkout holds the same files at another path.
mkdir $WORK/elsewhere/cmd/where $WORK/elsewhere/leaf $WORK/elsewhere/bare $WORK/elsewhere/other/part
cp go.mod $WORK/elsewhere/go.mod
cp cmd/where/main.go $WORK/elsewhere/cmd/where/main.go
cp leaf/leaf.go $WORK/elsewhere/leaf/leaf.go
cp bare/bare.go $WORK/elsewhere/bare/bare.go
cp other/go.mod $WORK/elsewhere/other/go.mod
cp other/part/part.go $WORK/elsewhere/other/part/part.go
cd $WORK/elsewhere
go list -export -f '{{.ImportPath}} {{.BuildID}}' ./... other.example/part
cmp stdout $WORK/first.txt

# Its vet reads the result the first checkout stored, and runs no tool.
go vet -x ./leaf
! stderr 'vet\.cfg'

# Its binary is linked again, and names this checkout.
go build -o $WORK/second.exe ./cmd/where
cd cmd/where
exec $WORK/second.exe
cd ../..

# A compile with -trimpath is that same compile. This package imports
# nothing, so no package of the standard library stands between the two keys.
go list -export -f '{{.BuildID}}' ./bare
cp stdout $WORK/bare.txt
go list -export -trimpath -f '{{.BuildID}}' ./bare
cmp stdout $WORK/bare.txt

# With -trimpath the link leaves the module path in the binary.
go build -trimpath -o $WORK/trimmed.exe ./cmd/where
cd cmd/where
exec $WORK/trimmed.exe -trimmed

-- go.mod --
module m

go 1.20

require other.example v0.0.0

replace other.example => ./other
-- cmd/where/main.go --
package main

import (
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"runtime"

	"m/leaf"
	"other.example/part"
)

var trimmed = flag.Bool("trimmed", false, "expect module paths in place of directories")

func main() {
	flag.Parse()
	_, file, _, _ := runtime.Caller(0)
	if *trimmed {
		expect(file, "m/cmd/where/main.go")
		expect(leaf.File(), "m/leaf/leaf.go")
		expect(part.File(), "other.example@v0.0.0/part/part.go")
		return
	}
	// The test runs this program in the directory of its package.
	here, err := os.Getwd()
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	root := filepath.Join(here, "..", "..")
	sameFile(file, filepath.Join(here, "main.go"))
	sameFile(leaf.File(), filepath.Join(root, "leaf", "leaf.go"))
	sameFile(part.File(), filepath.Join(root, "other", "part", "part.go"))
}

func expect(got, want string) {
	if got != want {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "the binary names %s, want %s\n", got, want)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}

func sameFile(got, want string) {
	gotInfo, err := os.Stat(got)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "the binary names %s, want %s: %v\n", got, want, err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	wantInfo, err := os.Stat(want)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	if !os.SameFile(gotInfo, wantInfo) {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "the binary names %s, want %s\n", got, want)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}
-- leaf/leaf.go --
package leaf

import (
	"runtime"

	"m/bare"
)

// File names the file this package was compiled from, as the binary records it.
func File() string {
	_, name, _, _ := runtime.Caller(bare.Zero())
	return name
}
-- bare/bare.go --
package bare

// Zero answers zero.
func Zero() int {
	return 0
}
-- other/go.mod --
module other.example

go 1.20
-- other/part/part.go --
package part

import "runtime"

// File names the file this package was compiled from, as the binary records it.
func File() string {
	_, name, _, _ := runtime.Caller(0)
	return name
}
